newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish state could float Enator stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish state could float Enator stake - paper.

text.p: The Swedish government could float the state's 25 percent stake of information technology company Enator, worth 1.4 billion crowns, on the Stockholm bourse, a business newspaper said on Thursday.
Dagens Industri said the Industry and Commerce Ministry had failed to find a buyer for its Enator shares before April 1 as planned and has extended the deadline by six weeks.
"It is taking a longer time than I thought to find a buyer," assistant under-secretary Per Tegner said.
"But the aim is that (the sale) will be finalised before the annual general shareholders' meeting on May 14. If we can't find a buyer, we will sell the shares on the stock market."
The float would most probably be the largest on the Stockholm bourse this year, the paper said.
The most likely buyer, Norwegian telephone company Telenor, recently declined to purchase the company, saying the price was at least 20 percent too high, the newspaper said.
"I don't want to comment on the price," Tegner told Dagens Industri. He said he would rather find one or two new main owners for Enator.
France Telecom, Global One, IBM and Siemens Nixdorf AG have also declined to buy the stake.
Enator has an annual turnover of 4.5 billion crowns and 5,000 employees.
